rationale: Round 1 compiled and ran correctly, so weights shift toward stronger obfuscation while respecting this benchmark's compute-bound profile (heapsort/accumulate template loops dominate runtime, and main holds 61% of text bytes). SUB is raised to the strongest weight: instruction substitution is cheap, safe, and its effect multiplies with every other pass on arithmetic-heavy code. ICALL and IGV stay high because indirect calls and global-variable encodings break static call/data-flow analysis of the many small template instantiations with low runtime risk. IBR is pushed up (0.7/0.65) since round 1 showed headroom for block-level indirection without breaking the build. SPLIT's diversity weight is raised to fragment the large main function, which amplifies FLA/BCF effectiveness at negligible runtime cost. FLA and BCF remain moderately weighted rather than maximal: flattening and bogus control flow carry the largest real runtime penalties in the tight inner loops that define this benchmark's execution time, so they are applied selectively where features favor security gain, keeping overall overhead acceptable. All CorrectnessRisk weights stay low to preserve the passing round-1 correctness result while still allowing feature-driven selection to apply every pass where the profile supports it.
